Convert and simplify expressions with units

Source: R/physics-units-util.R
convert_to.Rd

convert_to(expr, target_units, unit_system) rewrites the units and quantities of expr as products of powers of target_units (one unit, or a list of units) whenever the dimensions allow it, as SymPy's convert_to(). quantity_simplify() replaces prefixes by their values and units of the same dimension by one of them; with across_dimensions = TRUE it also converts to the preferred unit of the resulting dimension in unit_system. check_dimensions() returns expr when the terms of every sum agree in dimension, and raises a ValueError otherwise. find_unit() lists the names of the predefined units that contain a string, or that share the dimension of a unit, dimension or expression.

Usage

convert_to(expr, target_units, unit_system = "SI")

quantity_simplify(expr, across_dimensions = FALSE, unit_system = NULL)

check_dimensions(expr, unit_system = "SI")

find_unit(quantity, unit_system = "SI")

Arguments

expr

An expression.

target_units

A unit, a list of units, or a Tuple.

unit_system

A UnitSystem or its name.

across_dimensions

Combine units of different dimensions.

quantity

A string, quantity, dimension or expression.

Value

An expression, or a character vector for find_unit().

Examples

u <- physics_units()
convert_to(u$mile, u$kilometer)
#> 25146*kilometer/15625
convert_to(u$speed_of_light, list(u$meter, u$second))
#> 299792458*meter/second
quantity_simplify(u$kilo * u$foot * u$inch)
#> 250*foot^2/3
find_unit("volt")
#> [1] "volt"           "volts"          "electronvolt"   "electronvolts" 
#> [5] "planck_voltage"
